fluff.overview:
The CattleMaster is a twenty-five-ton IndustrialMech designed for livestock management on frontier agricultural worlds. The concept for rancher 'Mechs dates back to the twenty-fourth century, when colonists discovered that many garden worlds harbored large and sometimes dangerous native species alongside imported Terran livestock. Introduced in 3024 by Rastaban Agricultural on the Lyran Commonwealth world of Duran, the CattleMaster gave small ranching operations the ability to manage herds across vast planetary prairies.

Rugged enough for the harsh conditions of frontier ranching while remaining affordable for family-owned operations, the design proved an immediate success. The CattleMaster's popularity spread rapidly across Lyran agricultural worlds, becoming a fixture on planets like Cerillos, Galisteo, and Sierra, and making Rastaban Agricultural one of the most prolific IndustrialMech manufacturers in the Inner Sphere despite the company having no prior involvement in 'Mech production of any kind.
fluff.capabilities:
The CattleMaster's design philosophy prioritizes durability and operational independence over sophistication. The Rastaban Agro chassis is built to withstand the rigors of open-range work, including impacts from charging livestock and exposure to harsh weather conditions. Its Jones 100 internal combustion engine is a deliberate cost-saving choice, allowing operators to fuel the machine with locally refined petroleum products rather than depending on expensive fusion technology. The ability to use even the most unrefined fuels (including rendered animal byproducts) makes the CattleMaster remarkably self-sufficient in remote areas.

The cockpit layout borrows from the Chameleon training 'Mech, providing operators with familiar controls, though without military-grade electronics or an ejection seat. This design earns the CattleMaster its reputation as easy to pilot, making it accessible to ranchers with minimal training. Industrial armor plating protects the chassis from damage at the hands of an inexperienced operator or from a charging bull, while the 'Mech's ground speed of approximately sixty-five kilometers per hour keeps pace with most herd animals.

The base Herder configuration carries a retractable blade in the right arm for utility work and a powerful searchlight for operations in low-light conditions. A three-ton cargo bay in the left torso allows operators to carry supplies for extended periods away from their homesteads. The design particularly lacks any targeting systems, reflecting its purely civilian purpose.
fluff.history:
The CattleMaster's origins trace to the twenty-fourth century, when the first IndustrialMechs opened the door to large-scale ranching on colonial worlds. Species like the two-and-a-half-ton Odessan raxx proved far too large and dangerous for conventional animal husbandry, and the need for a purpose-built ranching 'Mech became apparent as humanity's demand for protein drove agricultural expansion across settled space. Rastaban Agricultural, already one of the Lyran Commonwealth's major grain exporters with holdings spanning trillions of acres across five worlds, recognized the market opportunity and introduced the CattleMaster in 3024.

The design found immediate success across Lyran agricultural worlds, spreading rapidly through the wealthy nation's extensive network of ranching planets. Whole generations grew up piloting CattleMasters on family haciendas, and it became common for young adults experienced with IndustrialMechs to later pursue military careers in regional militias and planetary guards. Though Rastaban Agricultural did not manufacture BattleMechs, the success of the CattleMaster made it one of the most prolific 'Mech manufacturers in the Inner Sphere, with the design's market primarily concentrated within the Lyran Alliance.

Rastaban Agricultural itself had an unusual economic position. Its largest grain customer was ironically the Draconis Combine, which purchased Commonwealth grain through third-party intermediaries to feed its population. The Lyran government encouraged this trade, adding to Rastaban's considerable revenues. The company's homeworld of Rastaban was lost to Clan Wolf during the Clan Invasion, though the CattleMaster production facility on Duran remained in Lyran hands throughout the upheavals of the thirty-first century.

The Jihad era brought an unexpected chapter in the CattleMaster's history. Faced with widespread destruction and a desperate shortage of SecurityMechs (particularly the Peacemaker) Rastaban Agricultural pivoted to producing a militarized variant in approximately 3072. This marked the company's first foray into dedicated military production. Following the Jihad's conclusion, the company reportedly scaled back militarized production, though the SecurityMech variant remained in service with planetary security forces.

The CattleMaster saw continued relevance well into the Dark Age. During the Liao Insurgency, Ijori Dè Guāng insurgents pressed CattleMasters and other IndustrialMechs into combat roles against Republic of the Sphere military forces, demonstrating the enduring utility of the design even in roles far beyond its original agricultural purpose.
fluff.deployment: The Herder is the primary production model of the CattleMaster, designed to transport all the stores and equipment needed to sustain an operator on the open range. Equipped with a retractable blade for utility work and a powerful searchlight for low-light operations, the Herder carries a three-ton cargo bay that allows ranchers to remain in the field for extended periods. The design lacks any weapons or targeting systems, relying entirely on its industrial tools and the operator's skill to manage livestock. Its simplicity and low operating cost have made it the standard choice for family ranching operations across the Lyran agricultural worlds where it sees the heaviest use.
